findings.text: non-blocking: no arm moves the review stamp while the code stamp holds, so a _review_stamp that returned a constant would keep all five tests green; the "or review changes" half of the node goal therefore has no assertion that fails if it regresses.

non-blocking: the assertion compares reviewed_head_sha of the selected review against the head the test itself wrote into the only review record it stored, so its only failing condition is that no acceptance judgement was reached; it cannot detect selection of a wrong record because no second record exists to select.

non-blocking: _review_stamp re-implements the sorted-key JSON sha256 digest owned by reckon/crew/plan_review.py:398-400 (_digest) with different separators, so a future change to the digest convention lands in one caller and not the other.

non-blocking: the comment says a subject line's own words do not read as a revision, but _REVISION_TOKEN matches any all-hex word of seven or more characters, so a subject containing such a word after the revision (a hash-like token, "defaced", "deadbeef") is returned by _delivered_revision as the head, and since the last match wins the real head is discarded and the run is silently skipped - the silent drop this commit exists to remove.
